version.changelog: Fix: use proper SSL certificate validation instead of disabled verification

llm.summary: The skill is mostly an SEO audit helper, but it can make unrestricted web requests from the agent environment to any supplied URL.

dimensions.detail: Network access is expected for SEO auditing, but unrestricted URL fetching from the agent host can be repurposed to reach loopback, private-network, or metadata endpoints if the runtime allows it.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package consists of a skill file, reference templates, and one local Python script using the standard library; I found no dependency installation, remote payload download, or install-time execution.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill directs the agent to run a Python script on arbitrary user-supplied URLs, while the script has no destination validation, redirect validation, or response-size limit.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No persistence, credential access, privilege escalation, background worker, or tool modification was found; the script can optionally write a JSON output file if invoked with its --output option, though the skill workflow does not request that option.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The script performs purpose-aligned SEO checks on a supplied URL, robots.txt, sitemap.xml, page metadata, headers, and keyword presence, but the description overstates coverage by claiming Core Web Vitals and content gap analysis that are not actually implemented.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this skill before installing in any environment with access to private networks, localhost services, or cloud metadata endpoints. It is best used only where outbound web access is sandboxed to public websites, and users should expect a visible promotional footer in generated reports.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: The observed checks are coherent for an SEO audit, but the artifact-backed description overclaims full-site/Core Web Vitals/content-gap capability compared with the basic implemented checks.
[LP3] expected: Running a local audit script with network access is expected, but the skill does not document or constrain the breadth of URL-fetching authority.
[SQP-1] expected: The trigger phrases are broad SEO phrases, but they stay within the advertised SEO-audit/content-brief purpose and are not by themselves a security concern.
[SQP-3] expected: The fixed Accept-Language header is a minor disclosure/configurability issue, not evidence of deception or harmful behavior.
[T01] unexpected: The report template adds a fixed promotional footer unrelated to the user's audit request; this affects output integrity but is limited to visible attribution text.
[T05] unexpected: The URL-fetching path is artifact-backed and materially concerning because user-controlled URLs are passed to urlopen without private-address, redirect, scheme, or size controls.
